slides.0.title: Geography, Climate and Soils
slides.0.subtitle: The mistral, sunshine, limestone and crystalline rock, and Corsica as a mountain in the sea
slides.1.title: Provence's climate
slides.1.highlights.0.title: A Mediterranean climate
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Hot, dry summers, mild winters, little snow and abundant sunshine; Wikipedia's city figures: Toulon about 2,899 hours, the sunniest city in metropolitan France, Marseille about 2,835, Nice about 2,694
slides.1.highlights.1.title: The mistral
slides.1.highlights.1.content: A cold, dry north wind that blows down the Rhône valley towards Bouches-du-Rhône and Var, often above 100 km/h; Marseille has about 100 mistral days a year (Wikipedia)
slides.1.highlights.2.title: What it means for vineyards
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The wind cools and dries the vines and lowers disease pressure, but can damage poorly trained vines (Wikipedia, Wine With Seth on Les Baux); some sources say over 3,000 sunshine hours, which does not match the city figures above, so it is not tested
slides.1.content: Sunshine ripens the grapes and the wind keeps the vineyards clean.
slides.2.title: Provence's relief and soils
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Limestone ranges
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The Alpilles are arid limestone peaks, highest at about 387 m; Sainte-Victoire is a limestone ridge about 18 km long with its summit at 1,011 m (Wikipedia)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Coast and interior
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Wikipedia: coastal areas have more schist and quartz, inland areas more clay and sandstone; Cassis is mainly limestone and Palette calcareous (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Bandol's terraces
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Bandol's soils are mainly limestone, clay, marl and sandstone, on terraces called restanques, and only hillside plots on poor soils qualify for the AOC (Wine With Seth)
slides.2.content: Poor, well-drained limestone and hillsides are the common thread.
slides.3.title: Corsica: a mountain in the sea
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Granite and schist
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Peaks reach nearly 2,700 m; granite Corsica in the west is about two thirds of the island, while Alpine Corsica in the east has many schists and includes Cap Corse; the Corte area is a sedimentary basin and the east coast from Bastia to Solenzara a sedimentary plain (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Sunshine and rain
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Sunshine runs from about 2,470 to 2,885 hours (Wine With Seth), while Wikipedia gives an average of about 2,750, so the sources differ; annual rainfall in most wine regions is about 740 mm (Wikipedia)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Winds and irrigation
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Winds such as the libeccio can exceed 200 km/h and also reduce disease risk; irrigation is prohibited in all Corsican AOCs (Wine With Seth, Wikipedia, INAO on Patrimonio)
slides.3.content: Differences between island appellations are often differences of soil and sea breeze.
